causal_chain: A candidate-local recommender that augments direct user-item affinity with a short-history intent encoder and a separately learned user residual memory introduces a new executable capability: persistent correction signals that are conditionally activated only when recent history indicates the relevant intent.

Because the proposal includes an explicit mechanism-off realization that preserves most components while disabling the residual contribution, any gain can be attributed more sharply to the residual-memory mechanism rather than incidental implementation changes.

If repeated ranking errors are caused by missing reusable correction state rather than only better negatives or regularization, the gated residual pathway should improve hard-positive recovery over a matched direct-affinity control.
The accepted context identifies a real gap: earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and an executable mechanism-off, so prior high-change ideas were hard to falsify cleanly.

The current executable family is dominated by static user/item embeddings or graph propagation variants, which do not provide an explicit reusable correction state for repeated pairwise mistakes concentrated in mixed-interest users.
blind_projection.closest_parent: The current profile is mechanistically weak because its user representation is fit as a largely static preference vector, so repeated pairwise mistakes on niche or temporally local interests do not become an explicit reusable correction signal. A descendant that maintains a learned user-level residual memory and gates it against a short-history intent encoder will better recover hard positives and improve full-sort ranking.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any observed improvement could come from merely adding capacity through extra parameters and a recent-history encoder, not from persistent user residual memory. Under that explanation, a matched model with the same short-history encoder and similar parameter count but with residual-memory contribution disabled should perform similarly.
discriminative_predictions: If gains come only from recent-history encoding, then disabling the residual-memory contribution while keeping the short-history encoder should largely preserve performance.

If persistent correction memory is the operative mechanism, the full model should outperform its mechanism-off control most strongly for users with diverse or conflicting training histories, where static representations are likeliest to blur intent.
If the hypothesis is wrong, the mechanism-off control and the full model should have similar full-sort NDCG@10 despite the added residual pathway.
expected_evidence: A measurable separation between the full model and its mechanism-off control on validation/test full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Ablation showing that zeroing residual memory at scoring time erodes any advantage that is present in the full model.
Larger relative gains on user subsets with higher historical item diversity or shorter-term preference shifts measured from train interactions only.
blind_projection.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if the matched mechanism-off control performs indistinguishably from or better than the full model on full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen protocol, especially if no stronger effect appears on mixed-interest users.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal requires a candidate-local recommender with a dual-state user representation: a persistent residual memory plus a short-history intent encoder, combined through a learned gate at scoring time. That introduces custom state construction and user-conditional fusion not available as a parameterized variant of the current executable profile's static MF or LightGCN operator families.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that combines direct user-item affinity with a gated user residual memory conditioned on a short recent-history intent encoder will rank held-out items better than a matched direct-affinity control, because repeated pairwise errors on niche or local interests become a persistent reusable correction signal instead of being absorbed into a single static user representation.
implementation_requirements: Build train-only per-user chronological interaction histories from the frozen training split.
Encode a fixed-length recent-history summary from item embeddings using a lightweight order-aware module such as gated averaging or a small GRU implemented in PyTorch.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender compatible with pairwise training and full-sort prediction.
Learn a separate user residual-memory embedding table and a gate that mixes direct user embedding, recent-history intent summary, and residual memory when scoring candidate items.
Provide an executable matched mechanism-off variant in the same codepath by forcing the residual-memory contribution to zero while retaining the same direct-affinity and recent-history components.
Support full-sort scoring for all items without accessing held-out interactions.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use the identical architecture, optimizer family, training data, and recent-history encoder, but set the residual-memory contribution to zero at train and inference time so the only removed mechanism is persistent user residual correction.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-state user model: a base user embedding for stable affinity, a learned persistent residual-memory vector for correction, and a gate driven by recent interacted item embeddings that decides how much residual correction should influence each candidate score.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Executable mechanism-off: keep the same item embeddings, base user embeddings, recent-history intent encoder, pairwise loss, and full-sort scorer, but deterministically clamp the residual-memory gate to zero and omit the residual-memory term from the score. This yields a matched direct-affinity-plus-recent-intent control without persistent correction memory.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add only one new mechanism beyond a matched direct-affinity-plus-recent-intent control: a learned persistent user residual-memory vector whose contribution is activated by a recent-history-conditioned gate during pairwise training and full-sort inference.
blind_projection.research_question: Does adding an explicit persistent user residual-memory pathway, gated by short recent-history intent, improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over a matched control that has recent-history context but no residual correction memory?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The model should fit within the stated development budget on ML-1M because it uses only embedding tables, a lightweight recent-history encoder, simple gating layers, and standard pairwise training; the main extra cost versus MF is train-only history caching and modest additional per-batch sequence aggregation.
